finding.statement: Let Y be a closed substack of X=M_{6,6}, A:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q), T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), and let q:A->T_Z be the surjection of FND-0180/FND-0168(3a) onto the kernel-form term. By FND-0185, A is a pure polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight -16, and polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category (FND-0033). Hence q splits, A is isomorphic to ker(q) direct-sum T_Z, and morphisms preserve canonical isotypic components, so writing A = A_Tate direct-sum A_nonTate for the canonical splitting into the Q(8)-isotypic part and its complement one gets (T_Z)_nonTate = q(A_nonTate). Therefore T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8) if and only if A_nonTate is contained in ker(q). Two lane consequences: a C66-TATE-SUPPORT proof routed through the verified interface source may replace the FND-0185 hypothesis 'A is Tate' by the strictly weaker and canonical 'A_nonTate is contained in ker(q)', and a C66-CEX-LOCAL / C66-CEX-SURVIVE disproof through the same interface must exhibit a non-Tate isotypic summand of A with nonzero image in T, which is the theorem's survival clause in checkable form. Exhibiting a non-Tate class anywhere in A, in an atlas, in a family base, or in a standalone product model settles neither lane.
